title: "The engineer of the future is the person who chooses what is worth doing." — Addy Osmani, Anthropic
talk_summary: Addy Osmani argues that as agents scale execution, the scarce resource becomes human judgment backed by evidence: the outer loop of deciding, verifying, approving, and owning stays with engineers. He names concrete failure modes (cognitive debt, cognitive surrender, orchestration tax) and proposes operational rules like 'explain it or don't ship it' and evidence-based review gates.

takeaways.technique: Evidence-bundle review gate instead of diff-glance
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents must return diffs, tests, logs, rationale, traces, and screenshots as a reviewable evidence bundle; the reviewer's job is to judge whether the evidence is sufficient, not to read every line.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Your agent returns evidence. It returns diffs, tests, logs, rationale, traces, trajectories, screenshots, whatever the work itself requires.

takeaways.technique: 'Explain it or don't ship it' ownership rule
takeaways.what_they_do: Require that some accountable party can explain the change and its risks before merge; treat unexplainable changes as blocked regardless of test pass.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Explain it or don't ship it. And it's not because humans have to type every line or read every line, but because someone has to understand the work well enough to defend it.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat human (and reviewer) attention as a non-parallelizable resource: design where review enters, what evidence is required, and what gets reused, instead of adding more parallel agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Your cognitive bandwidth does not parallelize. So, every loop that you create ends up causing more decisions to route, merge, verify, and integrate.

takeaways.what_they_do: Classify each edge (speed, recall, verification, taste) by how fast the frontier will erode it, and keep moving the team's edge up a level rather than defending a decaying capability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The strategy is not to cling to any one capability. It's for us to keep moving our edges up a level.

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain clean, readable repos not just for humans but because agents consume fewer tokens and cause fewer revisits on clean code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: clean and messy repos had roughly the same pass rates, but clean code actually used fewer tokens and caused fewer revisits
takeaways.numbers: Sonar study: clean vs messy repos roughly same pass rates; clean code used fewer tokens and caused fewer revisits (no figures given)

takeaways.what_they_do: Push verification into harnesses, evals, static checks, and model critique so review is cheaper, clearer, and harder to skip.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Verification is moving into harnesses, evals, static checks, and model critique.
